name: Wal. T. Osterhaut
bio: Wal. T. Osterhaut (also Osterhout) was a stockman with a ranch near Medora, where Johnny Goodall's newly bought cow-horses were taken in May 1884 to be put in condition for the round-up; in March 1884 the paper reported the death of the Osterhauts' baby. In April 1885 he served on a Little Missouri stockmen's committee, went to Miles City to arrange horses for Howard Eaton, and was listed as foreman of a round-up district. That September the association chairman proposed a present for him for his excellent work as foreman of the spring round-up, and in June 1886 a stray of his was found near Miles City.
